subject: GPU pool warmup delay causing elevated queuing — us-west-2 (OrbitAI)
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: James Patel <james.patel@orbitai.com>, ops@orbitai.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-08T09:12:00Z
Subject: GPU pool warmup delay causing elevated queuing — us-west-2 (OrbitAI)

Hi James / OrbitAI ops team,

Quick update: between 08:45–09:05 PDT this morning we observed a progressive increase in queue depth for your Dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2. Customers on your reserved pool experienced higher tail latency (95th percentile spiked to ~6s) and a handful of small inference requests were queued for up to ~90s while nodes completed driver initialization.

Impact: short-lived elevated latency for inference requests served from your Dedicated pool; no data loss and requests completed once warmup finished.

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Forced a rolling warm-restart of 3 recently added nodes to clear stuck init states.
- Routed new small-request traffic to a warm standby pool to reduce tail latency while we investigate.
- Enabled additional logging and captured driver/daemon traces (attached).

Next steps (short):
- We are triaging logs now and will follow up with a root-cause hypothesis within 2 business hours.
- If you want a targeted traffic shift back to primary pool, we can coordinate a controlled cutover.

I've opened a support ticket (4512) and attached the trace bundle. Apologies for the disruption — I know tail latency matters for your product.

Regards,
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Enterprise Cloud
Redwood Inference

Attachments: orbitai_support_ticket_4512.log, warmup-trace-20270408.tar.gz

A couple quick things from our side:

- Can you confirm whether this is related to the new node image rolled yesterday? We had a push at 01:00 UTC that added a new quantization profile.
- Also, what's ETA for a permanent fix vs a temporary routing bandaid? Our SLA window is tomorrow (10:00 PDT) and we need to be confident this won't reoccur under a similar warm scale event.

If helpful I can share sampler logs from our side (small footprint) — want to understand whether request patterns are magnifying the warmup behavior.

—James

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-08T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: GPU pool warmup delay causing elevated queuing — us-west-2 (OrbitAI)

Preliminary triage notes:
- Root cause hypothesis: a subset of newly provisioned nodes experienced a driver init race with the GPU health-check daemon. The daemon retried initialization repeatedly while the node reported as available to the allocator, which allowed requests to be scheduled to nodes that were not fully ready. That produced a gradual queue elevation instead of an immediate hard outage.
- Correlation with yesterday's image: the image includes a driver upgrade and an opportunistic quantization shim. The shim delays GPU context creation for a short period; combined with a timing window in the health-check, this created the stuck state on ~12% of new nodes.

Short-term mitigations we enacted (completed by 09:20 PDT):
- Forced warm-restart of affected nodes (cleared stuck init).
- Adjusted allocator to mark nodes as "ready-for-inference" only after health-check success (temporary stricter gating).
- Diverted small-request traffic to warm standby pool for 40 minutes while we validated behavior.

Next actions (owner / ETA):
- Full trace analysis (Marcus) — deliverable: detailed timeline and log slices (EOD today).
- Backout path for shim if required (Ben) — prepare candidate rollback within 24 hours.
- Deploy health-check gating change as a staged rollout to all regions (Chloe + infra team) — target 2027-04-09 03:00 UTC maintenance window; we will coordinate with Orbit ops.

I've attached the server-side trace bundle. We'll follow up with the post-incident remediation plan.

Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: James Patel <james.patel@orbitai.com>, ops@orbitai.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T17:30:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary & actions — warmup-induced queue elevation (OrbitAI — us-west-2)

Hi James / OrbitAI team,

Follow-up with the confirmed post-incident summary and next steps. Thanks for your patience while the infra team completed a deeper investigation. This email consolidates the timeline, root cause, customer impact, and our remediation schedule.

Summary of impact:
- Event window: 2027-04-08 08:45–09:20 PDT (ticket #4512).
- Symptom: progressive queue depth increase leading to 95th-percentile latency spike (~6s) for ~35 minutes. No request loss; all requests eventually served.

Root cause (confirmed):
- An interaction between the new node image's driver/quantization shim and the existing GPU health-check allowed nodes to be marked available before the GPU context completed initialization on a subset (~12%) of new nodes. The allocator then scheduled requests to those nodes, creating the observed warmup stalls and gradual queue elevation.

Remediation and timeline:
1) Applied shorter-term gating (completed 2027-04-08) — nodes require health-check pass before being advertised. (Owner: Platform Ops)
2) Backout-ready rollback for the quantization shim (prepared 2027-04-09) — will be executed if further regressions observed. (Owner: Ben Carter)
3) Health-check hardening & improved readiness probe (merged 2027-04-12, staged rollout across regions 2027-04-13–2027-04-16). (Owner: Marcus Lin)
4) Long-term: add proactive node warmup step and instrumentation to detect slow GPU context creation earlier (spec & ticket created; target Q2 release). (Owner: Infra Eng)

Customer-facing commitments:
- Planned maintenance window for canarying the hardened health-check in us-west-2: 2027-04-18 02:00–04:00 UTC. We'll perform canary gating on warm-standby nodes first and monitor for 2 hours before promoting the change.
- Credit proposal attached (credit-proposal-orbitai-20270408.pdf) covering partial SLA credit for the observed tail-latency impact; we are open to discussion if you prefer an alternate calculation.

Attached artifacts:
- Warmup traces and server logs captured during the event (warmup-trace-20270408.tar.gz)
- Ticket export and notes (orbitai_support_ticket_4512.log)
- Full postmortem draft (postmortem-warmup-20270415.md)

Action items for OrbitAI:
- Share sampler logs if you can (James) — will help validate whether request patterns amplified the incident.
- Confirm whether the proposed maintenance window works for your team or propose an alternative.

We're sorry for the disruption and appreciate the partnership while we tighten readiness and warmup behavior. If you'd like an on-call walkthrough of the traces, Marcus and Ben are available to join a 30–45 minute call this week.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Account Lead, Enterprise Cloud
Redwood Inference
